---
title: Publishing
---

A plugin is an ordinary Python distribution, so it goes to PyPI like any
other:

```bash
uv build
uv publish
```

## Names and dependencies

The distribution is `laplacekit-<name>` and the import package
`laplacekit_<name>`, where `<name>` is usually the library the plugin wraps:
`laplacekit-transformers` wraps `transformers`. The dependency on `laplacekit` should
match the record's `supports`, so that pip refuses an install the plugin can't
handle:

```toml
[project]
name = "laplacekit-mylib"
dependencies = ["laplacekit>=0.1a0,<0.2", "mylib>=2.1"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
```

The `[tool.pyright]` table turns on type checking in VS Code (Pylance), so a
class that misses a protocol method is marked in red for everyone who opens the
project. [Protocols in one page](protocols.py) shows what it catches.

Pin the wrapped library as tightly as the plugin needs. **laplacekit** itself
pins `curvlinops-for-pytorch==3.0.1`, since its KFAC adapter reads private
attributes of that version.

## Getting listed

The [plugin list](index.qmd) shows the plugins we know of. To add yours, open
a pull request on [the
repository](https://github.com/laplacekit/laplacekit) that adds one entry to
`docs/plugins/list.yml`:

```yaml
- title: laplacekit-mylib
  description: What it adds, in one sentence.
  categories: [Curvature]
  kind: third-party
  use: |
    import laplacekit as lk
    from laplacekit_mylib import MyCurvature

    post = lk.laplace(model, train_loader, likelihood=lk.Categorical(), hessian_approx=MyCurvature())
  guide: https://mylib.readthedocs.io/laplace
  source: https://github.com/me/laplacekit-mylib
  paper:
    text: Me et al., 2026
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/...
```

`categories` takes one kind from the table in the [Overview](overview.qmd),
`use` is the smallest code that uses the plugin, and `paper` is optional. The
list builds the install commands from `title`.
